# Pulse — Supabase

Schema reference only — the single source of truth is `schema.sql`. No application code lives here.

## Apply schema

Run `schema.sql` via the Supabase dashboard SQL editor or the `apply_migration` MCP tool. Safe to re-apply: tables use `CREATE TABLE IF NOT EXISTS`, RPCs use `CREATE OR REPLACE`, policies are `DROP ... IF EXISTS` before recreate.

---

## Tables

**`devices`** — one row per app install. UUID generated by the app on first launch; stable across FCM token rotations, resets on reinstall. All client writes go through SECURITY DEFINER RPCs (see below); the table carries no open RLS policy.

| Column       | Type                 | Notes                                                                         |
| ------------ | -------------------- | ----------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `id`         | UUID PK              | App-generated                                                                 |
| `fcm_token`  | TEXT NOT NULL        | UNIQUE (`devices_fcm_token_key`). Updated via `onTokenRefresh`                |
| `notify_at`  | TIME                 | Nullable — null = notify at cron time (MVP default); set = preferred UTC time |
| `user_id`    | UUID FK → auth.users | Stamped after login; nullable. `ON DELETE SET NULL`                           |
| `updated_at` | TIMESTAMPTZ          |                                                                               |

**`user_preferences`** — one row per authenticated user.

| Column        | Type                 | Notes                                            |
| ------------- | -------------------- | ------------------------------------------------ |
| `user_id`     | UUID PK → auth.users | RLS: `auth.uid() = user_id`. `ON DELETE CASCADE` |
| `preferences` | JSONB                | Full `UserPreferences` object. Default `'{}'`    |
| `updated_at`  | TIMESTAMPTZ          |                                                  |

**`digests`** — one row per region per date, shared across all users. Cron upserts on `(region, date)` — safe to re-run. Rows older than 7 days are evicted before each daily write. PK `(region, date)` covers the main app query (`WHERE region = ANY($1) AND date = $2`); max ~56 rows (8 regions × 7 days), no extra index.

| Column       | Type        | Notes                       |
| ------------ | ----------- | --------------------------- |
| `region`     | TEXT        | e.g. `"Hungary"`            |
| `date`       | DATE        | e.g. `2026-05-16`           |
| `payload`    | JSONB       | `{ headlines: Headline[] }` |
| `created_at` | TIMESTAMPTZ |                             |

**`notify_state`** — single-row store of the last window processed by `jobs/notify.ts`. The job notifies devices whose `notify_at` fell in `(last_run_at, now]`, so no device is dropped when the GitHub Actions schedule fires irregularly. Seeded with `now()` so the first run after deploy sees a tiny window (no mass-notify). Cron service-role only.

| Column        | Type        | Notes                                              |
| ------------- | ----------- | -------------------------------------------------- |
| `id`          | BOOLEAN PK  | `DEFAULT TRUE CHECK (id)` — forces exactly one row |
| `last_run_at` | TIMESTAMPTZ | `DEFAULT now()`                                    |

**`pipeline_runs`** — one row per daily-digest run; durable observability/cost record written by `jobs/daily-digest.ts` (see `cron/src/runReport.ts`, RunReport `pulse.run.v1`). Promoted scalar columns make cost-over-time queries cheap; the full structured report lives in `report`. Cron service-role only (no client read path).

| Column              | Type                   | Notes                                          |
| ------------------- | ---------------------- | ---------------------------------------------- |
| `id`                | BIGINT PK              | `GENERATED ALWAYS AS IDENTITY`                 |
| `run_at`            | TIMESTAMPTZ NOT NULL   | Indexed `DESC` (`pipeline_runs_run_at_idx`)    |
| `status`            | TEXT NOT NULL          |                                                |
| `total_cost_usd`    | NUMERIC(10,6) NOT NULL |                                                |
| `total_tokens`      | INTEGER NOT NULL       |                                                |
| `regions_succeeded` | SMALLINT NOT NULL      |                                                |
| `regions_failed`    | SMALLINT NOT NULL      |                                                |
| `duration_ms`       | INTEGER                | Nullable                                       |
| `report`            | JSONB NOT NULL         | Full per-region quality / cost / notify report |
| `created_at`        | TIMESTAMPTZ            | `DEFAULT now()`                                |

---

## RLS

Two-key model: publishable key in the app, secret (service-role) key server-side only. The service role bypasses RLS, so cron-only tables define no policy and stay private.

| Table              | Rule                                                                                                                   |
| ------------------ | ---------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `digests`          | SELECT open to all (`public read`, publishable key). Writes via secret key (bypasses RLS).                             |
| `devices`          | No open policy. RLS denies every direct anon/authenticated SELECT/INSERT/UPDATE. All client access via the RPCs below. |
| `user_preferences` | SELECT/INSERT/UPDATE restricted to `auth.uid() = user_id` (app publishable key).                                       |
| `notify_state`     | No policy — cron service-role only.                                                                                    |
| `pipeline_runs`    | No policy — cron service-role only.                                                                                    |

---

## RPCs (SECURITY DEFINER)

All client writes to `devices` go through these instead of direct table access, which lets the table stay fully RLS-locked.

| Function                               | Grant                             | Purpose                                                                                                                                      |
| -------------------------------------- | --------------------------------- | -------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `register_device(id, token, user_id?)` | anon, authenticated, service_role | Canonical registration write (app + cron). Upserts by stable `id`; evicts any other row holding the same token to collapse reinstall ghosts. |
| `update_notify_time(id, notify_at)`    | anon, authenticated, service_role | Only path for the app to change a device's `notify_at`. Returns `FOUND`.                                                                     |
| `link_device_to_user(id)`              | authenticated, service_role       | Stamps `auth.uid()` (not a parameter) onto a device row — caller can only link to self.                                                      |
| `peek_due_notifications()`             | service_role                      | Read-only "is any device due since `last_run_at`?". Used by the notify workflow guard.                                                       |
| `claim_due_notifications()`            | service_role                      | Returns due FCM tokens AND advances `last_run_at` atomically (`FOR UPDATE`, at-most-once).                                                   |

**Gotcha — anon auto-grant.** Supabase's `ALTER DEFAULT PRIVILEGES` auto-grants `EXECUTE` on every new public function directly to `anon` (and `authenticated`/`service_role`), so `REVOKE ... FROM PUBLIC` alone leaves `anon` able to call it. Service-only functions (`peek_due_notifications`, `claim_due_notifications`) and `link_device_to_user` therefore revoke from `anon` explicitly: `REVOKE EXECUTE ... FROM PUBLIC, anon[, authenticated]`.
